results.title: Boone–Higman theorem (easy direction)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi \colon F_n \to G$ be a surjective homomorphism from the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators onto a group $G$. If there are injective homomorphisms $G \to H$ and $H \to K$, where $H$ is a simple group and $K$ is a finitely presented group, then the word problem of $G$ with respect to $\varphi$ is solvable.

results.title: Kuznetsov's theorem on finitely presented simple groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple group, let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$ generators, and let $\varphi \colon F_n \to G$ be a surjective homomorphism whose kernel is the normal closure of finitely many elements. Then the word problem of $G$ with respect to $\varphi$ is solvable: there is an algorithm that decides, for every word $w$ in the $n$ generators and their inverses, whether $\varphi(w) = 1$.

results.title: Right orders on a group (Kourovka Problem 16.50)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The right orders of a group $G$ are the linear orders $\le$ on $G$, viewed as relations, that are invariant under right multiplication: $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 16.50 (finitely generated simple right-orderable groups)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there exists a finitely generated simple group $G$ admitting a right order, that is, a linear order $\le$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$. The problem is due to V. M. Kopytov and N. Ya. Medvedev.

results.title: Finitely generated simple right-orderable groups exist
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a finitely generated simple group $G$ that admits a right order, that is, a linear order $\le$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 16.50 positively.

results.title: Erdős Problem 198
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that the complement of every Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ contains an infinite arithmetic progression: for every Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ there are natural numbers $a$ and $d \ge 1$ such that $a + kd \notin A$ for every natural number $k$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 198 is false
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not the case that the complement of every Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ contains an infinite arithmetic progression: there is a Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that for all natural numbers $a$ and $d \ge 1$ some term $a + kd$, $k \in \mathbb{N}$, lies in $A$. Here $A$ is Sidon when $w + x = y + z$ with $w, x, y, z \in A$ forces $\{w, x\} = \{y, z\}$.

results.title: Multigraph state of Karger's algorithm
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A state over a vertex type $V$ consists of a list of current (super-)vertices in $V$ and a list of edges, each an ordered pair of elements of $V$; repeated pairs are parallel edges.

results.title: Valid multigraph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A multigraph, given by a list of vertices and a list of edges (pairs of vertices, with multiplicity), is valid when its vertex list has no repeated entries and every edge joins two distinct vertices of the list.

results.title: Size of a cut
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list of edges (pairs of vertices, repeated pairs counted with multiplicity) and a map $X$ from vertices to booleans, the size of the cut $X$ is the number of edges $(u, v)$ in the list with $X(u) \ne X(v)$.

results.title: Cuts of a multigraph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A map $X$ from vertices to booleans is a cut of a multigraph state $G$ when some vertex $v$ of $G$ has $X(v) = \mathrm{true}$ and some vertex $w$ of $G$ has $X(w) = \mathrm{false}$.

results.title: Minimum cut size
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $k$ is the minimum cut size of a multigraph state $G$ when some cut of $G$ has size $k$ and every cut of $G$ has size at least $k$.

results.title: Renaming a vertex
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For vertices $a$ and $b$, renaming $b$ to $a$ is the map on vertices that sends $b$ to $a$ and fixes every other vertex.

results.title: Edge contraction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a multigraph state $G$ and a pair of vertices $e = (a, b)$, the contraction of $G$ along $e$ deletes the first occurrence of $b$ from the vertex list, replaces $b$ by $a$ in both endpoints of every edge, and then deletes every edge whose two endpoints are equal.

results.title: Success probability of the contraction process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, a number $f$ of allowed contractions and a multigraph $G$ with edge list $E_G$, the probability $P_k(f, G)$ that the contraction process on $G$ returns $k$ is defined by recursion on $f$. If $f = 0$, or $G$ has at most two vertices, or $G$ has no edges, then $P_k(f, G)$ is $1$ when $G$ has exactly $k$ edges and $0$ otherwise. Otherwise…

results.title: Cut sizes under contraction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph state, $e = (a, b)$ a pair of vertices and $Y$ a map from vertices to booleans, and let $\rho$ send $b$ to $a$ and fix every other vertex. The size of the cut $Y$ in the contraction of $G$ along $e$ equals the size of the cut $Y \circ \rho$ in $G$.

results.title: Contraction preserves the minimum cut size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph state with minimum cut size $k$, and let $X$ be a cut of $G$ of size $k$. If $e = (a, b)$ is an edge of $G$ with $X(a) = X(b)$, then the contraction of $G$ along $e$ also has minimum cut size $k$.

results.title: Contraction preserves validity and removes one vertex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a multigraph $G$ is valid and $e$ is one of its edges, then the contraction of $G$ along $e$ is valid and has exactly one vertex fewer than $G$.

results.title: Handshake lemma
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a valid multigraph $G$, the sum over the vertices $v$ of $G$ of the number of edges crossing the singleton cut $\{v\}$ equals twice the number of edges of $G$.

results.title: Minimum cut size bounds the number of edges
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph state with $n \ge 2$ vertices, $m$ edges (counted with multiplicity) and minimum cut size $k$. Then $n k \le 2m$: every vertex has degree at least $k$, since its singleton is a cut.

results.title: The success probability is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, every number $f$ of allowed contractions and every multigraph state $G$, the probability $P_k(f, G)$ that the contraction process on $G$ returns $k$ satisfies $0 \le P_k(f, G)$.

results.title: The success probability is at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, every number of allowed contractions and every multigraph $G$, the probability that the contraction process on $G$ returns $k$ is at most $1$.

results.title: Karger's bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with $n \ge 2$ vertices and minimum cut size $k$. Then the contraction process on $G$, with $n$ contractions allowed, returns $k$ with probability at least $2 / (n(n-1))$.

results.title: Success probability of repeated runs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a multigraph $G$ with $n$ vertices and natural numbers $k$ and $t$, let $p$ be the probability that one run of the contraction process on $G$, with $n$ contractions allowed, returns $k$. The repeated success probability is $1 - (1 - p)^t$, the probability that at least one of $t$ independent runs returns $k$.

results.title: Repeating Karger's algorithm succeeds with probability at least one half
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph state with $n \ge 2$ vertices and minimum cut size $k$, and let $t$ be a natural number with $n(n-1) \le 2t$. Then the probability that at least one of $t$ independent runs of the contraction process returns $k$ is at least $1/2$.

results.title: Amplification with high probability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with $n \ge 2$ vertices and minimum cut size $k$, and let $c$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $c \cdot n(n-1) \le 2t$. Then the probability that at least one of $t$ independent runs of the contraction process on $G$ returns $k$ is at least $1 - (1/2)^c$.

results.title: Karger's algorithm succeeds with high probability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with $n \ge 2$ vertices and minimum cut size $k$, and let $t$ be a natural number with $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil \cdot n(n-1) \le 2t$. Then the probability that at least one of $t$ independent runs of the contraction process on $G$ returns $k$ is at least $1 - 1/n$.

results.title: Cuts distinct as partitions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two maps $X, Y$ from vertices to booleans are distinct on a list of vertices $S$ when some $v \in S$ has $X(v) \ne Y(v)$ and some $w \in S$ has $X(w) = Y(w)$; so on $S$ neither cut is the other or its complement.

results.title: Each minimum cut survives with probability at least $2/(n(n-1))$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with $n \ge 2$ vertices whose minimum cut size $k$ is at least $1$, and let $X$ be a cut of $G$ with exactly $k$ crossing edges. Then the probability that the contraction process on $G$, allowed up to $n$ contractions, outputs the cut $X$ is at least $2/(n(n-1))$.

results.title: Survival probabilities of distinct cuts sum to at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with vertex list $S$, let $f$ be a number of allowed contractions, and let $X_1, \dots, X_m$ be Boolean functions on the vertex type that are pairwise distinct as partitions of $S$. Then the probabilities that the contraction process on $G$, with $f$ contractions allowed, outputs $X_1, \dots, X_m$ add up to at most $1$.

results.title: At most $n(n-1)/2$ minimum cuts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At most $n(n-1)/2$ minimum cuts (Karger; Kleinberg and Tardos, Section 13.2). Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with $n \ge 2$ vertices whose minimum cut size $k$ is at least $1$. If $X_1, \dots, X_m$ are cuts of $G$, each with exactly $k$ crossing edges, that are pairwise distinct as partitions of the vertices of $G$, then $2m \le n(n-1)$, that is, $m \le n(n-1)/2$.

results.title: Homozygosity recursion in the infinite-alleles model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: One generation of drift and mutation in the infinite-alleles model with `M` gene copies and mutation probability `u` per copy: `F' = (1 - u)² (1/M + (1 - 1/M) F)`. The model domain is `2 ≤ M` (two distinct copies must exist) and `0 ≤ u ≤ 1`; the theorems below assume only `1 ≤ M`, and `M = 1` is an algebraic extension with no biological meaning. For `M = 0` the definition uses the junk value `1/0 = 0`.

results.title: Equilibrium homozygosity in the infinite-alleles model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The equilibrium homozygosity `F* = (1 - u)² / (M - (M - 1)(1 - u)²)`. Biologically meaningful for `2 ≤ M`; its denominator is positive for `1 ≤ M` and `0 < u ≤ 1`, the hypotheses of the theorems below (`M = 1` being an algebraic extension).

results.title: Equilibrium homozygosity is a fixed point of the recursion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `F*` is a fixed point of the homozygosity recursion.

results.title: Uniqueness of the equilibrium homozygosity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `0 < u ≤ 1`, `F*` is the unique fixed point of the homozygosity recursion.

results.title: Convergence of homozygosity to equilibrium
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `0 < u ≤ 1` the homozygosity converges to `F*` from every initial value `F₀`.

results.title: Kimura–Crow limit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With `M = 2N` gene copies and mutation probability `u = θ/(4N)` (so that `θ = 4Nu`), the equilibrium homozygosity tends to `1/(1 + θ)` as `N → ∞`.

results.title: Limit $\theta/(1+\theta)$ of the equilibrium heterozygosity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The equilibrium heterozygosity `H* = 1 - F*` tends to `θ/(1 + θ)` as `N → ∞` with `M = 2N` and `u = θ/(4N)`.

results.title: Auxiliary row computation for the Smith–Waterman table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The cells `H[i+1][j+1], H[i+1][j+2], …` of a row from the remaining letters `b :: ys` of the second sequence, the remaining cells `up :: prev` of the previous row, the previous row's cell `diag` to the upper left and the cell `left` just computed. A previous row that is too short ends the row early (this does not happen for rows of the table, `nextRow_eq`).

results.title: Next row of the Smith–Waterman table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The row of the table for the prefix extended by `a`, from the previous row: `H[i+1][0] = 0`, then the recurrence left to right.

results.title: Row-by-row filling of the Smith–Waterman table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Smith–Waterman table, filled row by row over the remaining letters of the first sequence: `row` is the current row and `best` the largest cell of the earlier rows.

results.title: The Smith–Waterman table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The largest cell of the `(|xs| + 1) × (|ys| + 1)` table, with the zero row `H[0][j] = 0` to start.

results.title: One row of the table
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: From the row of the prefix `px`, `nextRow` computes the row of `px ++ [a]`: the cells `H[i+1][j] = swCellScore σ gap (px ++ [a]) py` for the prefixes `py` of `ys`, shortest first.

results.title: The table computes the Smith–Waterman score
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `swTab` is the largest cell `swCellScore σ gap px py` over all pairs of prefixes.

results.title: The table computes the optimal local alignment score
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The table computes the optimal local alignment score (Smith–Waterman 1981, `gap ≤ 0`): `swTab` is the maximum, over all pairs of infixes of `xs` and `ys` (including the empty ones, which give the floor `0`), of their optimal global alignment score `nwScore`.
